For the production function q=z11/3z22/3q = z_1^{1/3} z_2^{2/3}q=z11/3​z22/3​, compute the MRTS at (z1,z2)=(2,8)(z_1, z_2) = (2, 8)(z1​,z2​)=(2,8).

MRTS=αβz2z1MRTS = \frac{\alpha}{\beta}\frac{z_2}{z_1}MRTS=βα​z1​z2​​
  • Isoquants
Show solution
  1. Plug into the formula: MRTS=1/32/3⋅82=12⋅4=2MRTS = \frac{1/3}{2/3} \cdot \frac{8}{2} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 4 = 2MRTS=2/31/3​⋅28​=21​⋅4=2.
  2. So the isoquant slope is −2-2−2: cutting z1z_1z1​ by one unit needs about two more units of z2z_2z2​ to hold output constant.

3Medium

For C(q)=40+30q−4q2+12q3C(q) = 40 + 30q - 4q^2 + \tfrac{1}{2}q^3C(q)=40+30q−4q2+21​q3, find the output minimizing average variable cost and the marginal cost there.

AVC(q)=a+bq+cq2AVC(q) = a + bq + cq^2AVC(q)=a+bq+cq2
  • Cost Curves
Show solution
  1. AVC(q)=(C(q)−40)/q=30−4q+0.5q2AVC(q) = (C(q) - 40)/q = 30 - 4q + 0.5q^2AVC(q)=(C(q)−40)/q=30−4q+0.5q2. From AVC′(q)=−4+q=0AVC'(q) = -4 + q = 0AVC′(q)=−4+q=0, q=4q = 4q=4.
  2. AVC(4)=30−16+8=22AVC(4) = 30 - 16 + 8 = 22AVC(4)=30−16+8=22, and with MC(q)=30−8q+1.5q2MC(q) = 30 - 8q + 1.5q^2MC(q)=30−8q+1.5q2, MC(4)=30−32+24=22MC(4) = 30 - 32 + 24 = 22MC(4)=30−32+24=22 — the MC curve passes exactly through the AVC minimum.

Hard

4Hard

Let α=0.3\alpha = 0.3α=0.3, β=0.4\beta = 0.4β=0.4 (decreasing returns), w1=w2=1w_1 = w_2 = 1w1​=w2​=1. Compute c(w,16)/c(w,8)c(w, 16)/c(w, 8)c(w,16)/c(w,8) from the conditional-demand formula, explain why it exceeds 222, and state the degree of homogeneity of c(w,q)c(w, q)c(w,q) in qqq in general.

c(w,tq)=t1/(α+β) c(w,q)c(w, tq) = t^{1/(\alpha+\beta)}\, c(w, q)c(w,tq)=t1/(α+β)c(w,q)
  • Cost Minimization
  • Isoquants
Show solution
  1. With s=α+β=0.7s = \alpha + \beta = 0.7s=α+β=0.7, z1(w,q)=[q⋅K]1/sz_1(w, q) = [q \cdot K]^{1/s}z1​(w,q)=[q⋅K]1/s (where K=(αw2/βw1)βK = (\alpha w_2/\beta w_1)^\betaK=(αw2​/βw1​)β is independent of qqq), so z(w,q)z(w, q)z(w,q) is homogeneous of degree 1/s1/s1/s in qqq — and so is c(w,q)=w⋅z(w,q)c(w, q) = w \cdot z(w, q)c(w,q)=w⋅z(w,q).
  2. Hence c(w,16)/c(w,8)=21/0.7≈2.69c(w, 16)/c(w, 8) = 2^{1/0.7} \approx 2.69c(w,16)/c(w,8)=21/0.7≈2.69. Under decreasing returns, doubling output needs more than double the inputs, so cost more than doubles. In general c(w,q)c(w, q)c(w,q) is homogeneous of degree 1/(α+β)1/(\alpha+\beta)1/(α+β) in qqq.
